title: Documentation Standards by Tier — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
The documentation a request for **Hardship and Protective Holds** relies on is fixed by tier: whether documentation must be received before approval, what kind it is, how long the consumer has to supply it, how often an incomplete package may be resubmitted, whether income records are needed and what income drop qualifies, and the channels through which documentation is accepted.

## Standards

| Tier | Documentation required before approval | Documentation kind | Documentation due days | Resubmissions allowed | Months of income records | Minimum documented income drop | Channels accepted for documentation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | No | Self-attestation | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.0% | None |
| Documented Hardship Hold | Yes | Income loss evidence | 15 | 1 | 2 | 20.0% | Online portal, email, mail, fax |
| Disaster Relief Hold | Yes | Disaster-area residence proof | 30 | 1 | 0 | 0.0% | Online portal, email, mail, fax |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | Yes | Financial assistance application | 30 | 1 | 0 | 0.0% | Online portal, email, mail, fax |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | Yes | Medical or disability certification | 21 | 1 | 3 | 30.0% | Online portal, mail, fax |
| Military Service Hold | Yes | Active-duty status proof | 30 | 1 | 0 | 0.0% | Online portal, email, mail, fax |

## Column notes

1. **Documentation required before approval** — whether documentation must be received before the hold is approved.
2. **Documentation kind** — the documentation the tier relies on: self-attestation, income loss evidence, disaster-area residence proof, financial assistance application, medical or disability certification, or active-duty status proof.
3. **Documentation due days** — calendar days after the request within which documentation must arrive; 0 where none is required.
4. **Resubmissions allowed** — times incomplete documentation may be resubmitted before the request is denied.
5. **Months of income records** — months of income records required with the documentation; 0 where income records are not required.
6. **Minimum documented income drop** — the smallest documented drop in household income that qualifies, in percent; 0.0 where the tier does not test income.
7. **Channels accepted** — the channels through which documentation is accepted; empty where none is required.

## Points of reading

- Only two tiers test income: the Documented Hardship Hold (a drop of at least 20.0% shown by 2 months of records) and the Long-Term Hardship Hold (a drop of at least 30.0% shown by 3 months of records).
- The Long-Term Hardship Hold does not accept documentation by email; its documentation channels are the online portal, mail and fax.
- The 30-Day Hardship Pause requires no documentation, has no documentation channel and allows 0 resubmissions.
